role_progression.title: Senior UX Engineer
role_progression.summary: Joined Podium as Senior UX Engineer, contributing to Stencil components, design tokens, inputs, and the path toward the first stable releases.

role_progression.title: Tech Lead
role_progression.summary: Stepped into Tech Lead before the v2.0 release, driving the React rewrite, release strategy, and growing contributor involvement — including Matjaž Drolc and Dorin Avasiloaei as the controlled direction took shape.

meta.purpose: Portable Podium case-study timeline for a personal website. No Podium package dependencies — plain JSON only. Event types include contribution, release, milestone, team, infrastructure, context, field (off-site workshops/presentations), and fix (grouped bug-fix clusters).
meta.overview: From 2023 to 2026, Podium moved through six major eras — each one a deliberate architectural shift. I joined as Senior UX Engineer during the Stencil web-components monorepo, helped ship v1.0, then led the React rewrite and v2.0 release as Tech Lead. The library shed its Stencil roots, adopted controlled React patterns, migrated to Mantine UI while mentoring new contributors, and finally gained an MCP server for AI-assisted documentation. Click any era below to focus the timeline on that chapter.

milestones.title: Stencil Web Components Era
milestones.summary: Podium began as a Stencil-based design system shared across React, Vue, and Angular product teams. As Senior UX Engineer, I joined early and helped shape tokens, inputs, and the first stable release.
milestones.description: The library shipped as a Lerna monorepo with Stencil web components at its core. React, Vue, and Angular packages were generated wrappers around shadow-DOM components. Storybook documented components with slot-based composition (e.g. leading-icon slots, optionsMenu children).
milestones.outcome: Established the first stable public API (v1.0.0) and a cross-framework component foundation used by multiple Sportradar product teams.
milestones.collaborator_context: Dik Medvešček Murovec, Jure Tovornik, and SPORTRADAR\d.murovec drove early packaging, Storybook, and Lerna publishing before and alongside my contributions.

events.title: Podium journey anchor — v0.19.1 packaging
events.summary: The design system was already a multi-framework monorepo when I joined the company, built on web components and Lerna independent versioning.
events.description: Commit fda68ef43 (PD-807) updated packaging at v0.19.1. The repo contained Stencil core, react-library, vue-library, and angular-workspace packages with stencil build output targets.

events.title: First contribution — semantic color tokens (PD-827)
events.summary: I made my first commit to Podium, extending the design token system with new semantic color scales.
events.description: Commit 64ec6f105 added soft and mild semantic color SCSS includes (PD-827), establishing my early focus on design tokens and Stencil-era styling foundations.

events.title: Norway trip — Boomers team stakeholder presentation
events.summary: I travelled to Norway to present Podium to the Boomers team, one of the first external product teams adopting the design system for a large-scale sports data collection application.
events.description: The Boomers team was building a high-stakes in-game sports data collection product. This was one of the earliest stakeholder presentations of Podium outside of core Sportradar, establishing the library's first real-world adoption signal and validating its direction before v1.0.0 shipped.

events.title: v1.0.0 — first major stable release
events.summary: Podium shipped its first major version, giving product teams a versioned, documented design system for the first time.
events.description: Lerna publish commit 15e3b9112 marked v1.0.0. The Stencil monorepo with React/Vue/Angular wrappers established the first stable public API surface and ended the pre-1.0 experimental phase.

events.title: Stencil Select — slot-based web component API
events.summary: Select was a web component composed with menu slots and a leading-icon slot — the pattern every framework wrapper inherited.
events.description: At commit 15e3b9112, PdsSelect used shadow DOM with slot="leading-icon" and a PdsMenu / PdsMenuOption children tree. This era anchor is documented in repository-archaeology select-stencil-era snippets.

events.title: Loader component — animation, sizes, and colors
events.summary: I designed and shipped the Loader component with configurable speed, size, and color — one of the first components I owned end-to-end.
events.description: Implemented PdsLoader with PdsVelocity prop, size and color variants, Storybook stories, and Stencil test scaffolding. Also fixed keyboard accessibility (tabindex) on disabled elements across menu and switch.

events.title: Clear functionality across input family
events.summary: I added a consistent clear-button pattern to TextField, TextArea, Select, and Autocomplete so users could reset fields in one action.
events.description: Batch of commits on 2023-08-31 added clear-value methods and UI to TextField, TextArea, Select, and Autocomplete Stencil components — improving form UX consistency across the input family.

events.title: Keyboard accessibility fixes — Menu and Switch
events.summary: I fixed keyboard accessibility across the Menu and Switch components, ensuring disabled elements could not be tabbed into.
events.description: Commit 5b0e7c808 removed the option of tabbing into disabled elements. Related fixes on menu-option tabindexes and switch disabled state improved keyboard navigation across the Stencil input family.

events.title: PdsTable for React — first React-native table package
events.summary: I started moving beyond Stencil wrappers by shipping a React-native table package for product teams that needed data-heavy UIs.
events.description: feat/PD-1135 introduced react-table-dk (later renamed react-table), signaling early exploration of React-first components outside the Stencil generation pipeline.

milestones.title: Last Stencil Releases (v1.22.x)
milestones.summary: Stencil components reached their final releases while, as Senior UX Engineer, I helped prepare the migration path as a parallel React-first rewrite branch opened — the bridge to Podium 2.0.
milestones.description: v1.22.x was among the last significant Stencil publishes. Simultaneously, the react-custom-components branch began replacing wrapper-generated components with hand-written React. A legacy package naming scheme was introduced to ease consumer migration.
milestones.outcome: Maintained Stencil consumers on v1.22.x while preparing the React-first migration path and legacy package aliases.
milestones.collaborator_context: Dik Medvešček Murovec published the final Stencil releases and opened the react-custom-components branch that became the v2.0 foundation.

events.title: v1.22.0 — last significant Stencil publish
events.summary: This was one of the final Stencil-era releases before the library pivoted fully to React.
events.description: Lerna publish 55dd978e3 tagged @podium-design-system/web-components@1.22.0. Stencil components remained the primary distribution while React-first work proceeded on a parallel branch.

events.title: Gera visit — Transformers team workshop & DX reckoning
events.summary: I visited the Transformers team in Gera to run a hands-on developer workshop on Podium adoption. We discovered two critical problems — Shadow DOM style lock-in and an overly complex composition API — that became the direct push for the React rewrite and the shift to prop-based component APIs.
events.description: The workshop exposed two severe DX failures. First, Stencil's Shadow DOM made it impossible to style components from the outside without CSS variable workarounds — a blocker for product teams with their own design requirements. Second, the composition-heavy slot API forced developers to write verbose trees of nested components (PdsMenu > PdsMenuSection > PdsMenuOption) for even basic interactions, producing boilerplate that felt foreign to React developers. These findings gave concrete evidence to push for a full React rewrite and a shift in API philosophy: icons and options would become props rather than composed children, content would be generated and provided by the design system rather than assembled by consumers. This directly influenced the react-custom-components branch that opened in January 2024 and the prop-based API patterns that followed.

events.title: react-custom-components branch established
events.summary: A parallel branch was opened to rebuild components as native React instead of Stencil wrappers — the technical foundation for v2.0.
events.description: Commit afb8279a0 set up initial configuration for react custom components. Angular and Vue Stencil outputs were removed; the repo began hosting both legacy wrapped and new React-first components side by side.

events.title: Legacy package naming for v2.0 migration
events.summary: I introduced legacy package aliases so consumer teams could migrate to Podium 2.0 without breaking their existing imports overnight.
events.description: Commit 012d6fea1 added @podium-design-system/legacy-react-components and legacy-web-components package naming, providing a staged migration path from Stencil wrappers to React-first components.

milestones.title: React-First Rewrite & v2.0 Release
milestones.summary: I stepped into Tech Lead before v2.0 shipped, driving the React rewrite — rebuilding the library from Stencil wrappers into native React components and leading the release to Podium 2.0.
milestones.description: The react-custom-components branch replaced Stencil-generated wrappers with composed React components (trigger + optionsMenu pattern). Davor transitioned from Senior UX Engineer to Tech Lead around May 2024 while driving beta releases, className utilities, event API normalization, Drawer/Checkbox/Table work, and Storybook addon-docs integration. v2.0.0 published 2024-07-08 via Lerna.
milestones.outcome: Shipped @podium-design-system/react-components@2.0.0 — a breaking, React-only design system with ~20 components and a documented migration path from legacy packages.
milestones.collaborator_context: Dik Medvešček Murovec co-drove CI, Lerna versioning, and the final v2.0 merge. Jure Tovornik contributed Toast, Datepicker, Card, and Skeleton on the same branch.

events.title: Senior UX Engineer → Tech Lead
events.summary: I took on the Tech Lead role while leading the React rewrite toward v2.0 — setting direction, release strategy, and technical standards for the team.
events.description: Around May 2024, during the v2.0 beta release cycle (alpha.9 through beta.1), Davor assumed Tech Lead responsibilities for the Podium library. This preceded the v2.0.0 release on 2024-07-08 and coincided with growing contributor involvement as the controlled direction later attracted Matjaž Drolc, Dorin Avasiloaei, and Patryk Musiala.

events.title: Pure React Select — composed trigger + optionsMenu
events.summary: Select became a native React component: a trigger field with a dropdown menu composed as children, replacing the Stencil web component.
events.description: At commit a653eb159, PdsSelect used a React trigger + PdsMenu / PdsMenuOption composition. Still largely uncontrolled internally. Documented in repository-archaeology select-react-era snippets.

events.title: React Autocomplete — first searchable input after migration
events.summary: Autocomplete did not exist in the Stencil era; I introduced it as a searchable variant of the text field + menu pattern.
events.description: Commit c329e5ea8 added PdsAutocomplete with filter-as-you-type over an optionsMenu slot — same mental model as Select plus search. Documented in repository-archaeology autocomplete-react-era snippets.

events.title: Prop-based API shift — from composition slots to developer-friendly props
events.summary: Applying the lessons from Gera, I redesigned component APIs in the React rewrite — icons became props, event callbacks returned consistent types, and className utilities let consumer teams apply custom styles without fighting the library.
events.description: Following the Gera workshop findings, the React rewrite moved away from Stencil slot composition toward prop-based APIs. Icons shifted from slot children to props (leadingIcon on React Select at a653eb159). className utilities (d7e5bb8b0) replaced slot-based styling overrides. Event callbacks were normalized to return void instead of boolean (7da72af64). The library began generating and providing more structure internally so consumers wrote less boilerplate — a direct response to the composition-heavy DX problems observed in Gera.

events.title: v2.0 beta releases (alpha.9 → beta.1)
events.summary: I published a series of pre-release versions so consumer teams could test the React rewrite before the official 2.0 launch.
events.description: Multiple Lerna publishes between 2024-05-09 and 2024-05-30 (alpha.9 through beta.1) on the react-custom-components branch. Included className fixes, event API changes (void instead of boolean returns), and Storybook addon-docs.

events.title: v2.0 beta fix wave — Drawer, Table, Notification, Modal, Button
events.summary: During the v2.0 beta cycle I resolved a wave of migration bugs — Drawer API changes, Table overflow, Notification classNames, Modal style bleed, and Button disabled state — validating each with consumer feedback before the final release.
events.description: Pre-release fixes across May 2024: Drawer show/width API and onClick-outside events (10b3a9b6b), Table overflow and rounded corners (d332c1ca0), Notification classNames for embedded icons (16ff04e29), Modal wrapper style bleed prevention (32048fbf0), and Button disabled click-through (b4bc8769f). Each fix addressed real consumer pain discovered during beta adoption.

events.title: v2.0.0 RELEASE — React-first design system
events.summary: Podium 2.0 shipped — a full React library replacing years of Stencil web-component wrappers. This was the most important release in the project's history.
events.description: Lerna publish e8fa5e4b6 released @podium-design-system/react-components@2.0.0. The react-custom-components branch merged to master. Breaking change: consumers migrated from Stencil wrappers to direct React imports with legacy package aliases for gradual adoption.

milestones.title: Controlled Components & Stencil Removal
milestones.summary: As Tech Lead, I drove the Controlled direction after v2.0 — lifting form state to parent components — while Matjaž Drolc and Dorin Avasiloaei ramped up as core contributors and Stencil was removed entirely.
milestones.description: Introduced PdsSelectControlled and PdsMultiSelectControlled with explicit selectedOption/onMenuOptionSelect props. FilterChip received post-v2.0 fixes and Playwright coverage. Stencil was fully removed (a254c63f6). TextField gained error/validation states. Matjaž Drolc and Dorin Avasiloaei became highly active contributors under Tech Lead direction — token docs, CI, style alignment, and visual regression tests.
milestones.outcome: React-only codebase with controlled variants for form-heavy consumers; Stencil build pipeline eliminated; v2.3.0–2.3.1 releases; expanded contributor team under established Tech Lead leadership.
milestones.collaborator_context: Matjaž Drolc and Dorin Avasiloaei became the most active collaborators during this period — aligning Select/TextField styles, adding visual regression tests, and improving CI and token documentation while Davor led the controlled component direction.

events.title: Matjaž Drolc and Dorin Avasiloaei ramp up as core contributors
events.summary: Under Tech Lead direction, Matjaž and Dorin became the most active collaborators — improving CI, token docs, and component quality across the library.
events.description: From October 2024, Matjaž Drolc contributed TextField visual regression tests, Select/TextField style alignment, and Menu scrollbar fixes. Dorin Avasiloaei improved Storybook CI, token installation docs, and deployment infrastructure. Both worked within the controlled-direction goals set during Tech Lead tenure.

events.title: FilterChip — post-v2.0 fixes and Playwright coverage
events.summary: I fixed FilterChip surfaces and icons after the v2.0 migration and added visual regression tests to lock in the design.
events.description: Commits between 2024-08-13 and 2024-08-28 on fix/PD-misc-fix-pds-filter-chip: Playwright snapshots, leading/trailing icon tests, surface fixes for number badges at high intensity, and alignment corrections across components.

events.title: Controlled Select — explicit parent state API
events.summary: Select gained a Controlled variant so form builders could own the selected value and wire it to their state management.
events.description: Commit 2909c8934 introduced PdsSelectControlled with selectedOption and onMenuOptionSelect props, lifting selection state to the parent for forms and data binding. Documented in repository-archaeology select-controlled-era snippets.

events.title: Stencil fully removed from codebase
events.summary: The Stencil build pipeline and all web-component source were deleted — Podium became a pure React library.
events.description: Commit a254c63f6 removed Stencil configuration, generated outputs, and wrapper packages. Merged via feat/PD-misc-react-only. This closed the Stencil era permanently.

events.title: TextField error and validation states
events.summary: I added error feedback to TextField so forms could show validation messages inline — a key controlled-era UX improvement.
events.description: Commits on feat/PD-misc-text-field-error-state added feedbackStatus and feedbackMessage props, error state styling, and line-height corrections to PdsTextField.

events.title: helperText utility — TextField and TextArea validation messaging
events.summary: I introduced a reusable helperText utility for TextField and TextArea, then locked in its behaviour with Vitest snapshots and surface-aware visual regression tests.
events.description: Commits 4d3226311, 354a7620c, and c82fcd3c5 introduced a global helperText util, implemented it on PdsTextField and PdsTextArea, and added Vitest snapshots for neutral helper icons and surface variants. Issue-report modal dismiss button was also corrected (fa7208d07).

events.title: v2.3.1 release — post-Stencil stabilization
events.summary: A stabilization release after Stencil removal, with style alignment across Select, TextField, and controlled variants.
events.description: Release version 2.3.1 (73f473542) merged dev to master with TextField placeholder fixes, Select style alignment, Menu scrollbar fix, and token installation docs from collaborators.

milestones.title: Mantine UI Foundation & Team Growth
milestones.summary: As Tech Lead, I led the Mantine direction — rebuilding inputs on Mantine's accessible primitives — and mentored Maja Hladnik as she joined and became a core contributor.
milestones.description: Mantine UI was adopted as the new component foundation. PdsMantineAutocomplete launched the direction (commit 323a657ac). PodiumProvider replaced MantineWrapper. Maja Hladnik joined Feb 2025 (first commit 5d4d90348) and shipped MantineAutocomplete, icon tooling, and CI improvements under mentorship. Figma Code Connect work began Jul 2025.
milestones.outcome: Mantine-based input family (Autocomplete, Text, Menu, Button variants), PodiumProvider wrapper, and a growing contributor (Maja) mentored into core Mantine component ownership.
milestones.collaborator_context: Maja Hladnik joined in February 2025 and quickly took ownership of MantineAutocomplete, icon generation, and CI — mentored by Davor throughout the Mantine migration.

events.title: Maja Hladnik joins Podium — mentoring begins
events.summary: Maja joined the project and I began mentoring her on the design system codebase, testing patterns, and component conventions.
events.description: Maja Hladnik's first commit 5d4d90348 (2025-02-06) was SCSS deprecation fixes across TabGroup, FilterChipGroup, and other components — her entry point into the controlled-era codebase before the Mantine migration.

events.title: Mantine Autocomplete — new component foundation direction
events.summary: The team adopted Mantine UI as the foundation for new inputs, starting with Autocomplete — a flat data array instead of menu slots.
events.description: Commits 323a657ac and 17b37a0f3 introduced PdsMantineAutocomplete using Mantine Combobox with a data prop, clearable, and Podium styling. Replaced the optionsMenu slot pattern. Documented in repository-archaeology autocomplete-mantine-era snippets.

events.title: PodiumProvider — unified Mantine context wrapper
events.summary: I replaced the ad-hoc MantineWrapper with a single PodiumProvider that every Mantine component depends on.
events.description: Commit 40fc0e4da created PodiumProvider, moved @mantine/core and @mantine/hooks to peerDependencies, and exported pds-mantine.styles. Standardized how consumer apps wrap Mantine components.

events.title: FilterChip updated for Mantine era
events.summary: FilterChip was refreshed to align with the new Mantine-based input styling and testing infrastructure.
events.description: Vitest snapshot updates and FilterChip styling adjustments (ada2301c2) aligned the chip component with Mantine-era normalize styles and Playwright coverage patterns.

events.title: Figma Code Connect integration begins
events.summary: I started bridging Figma designs to code with Code Connect mappings so designers and developers shared a single source of truth.
events.description: feat/PDS-misc-figma-code-connect branch: Davor added Code Connect for Dropdown and ToggleButton; Maja added mappings for Text, Avatar, Badge, Divider, Tab, Breadcrumb, Box, Tag, Notification, Backdrop, and MantineAutocomplete.

events.title: Mantine Select — flat data, searchable, clearable
events.summary: Select completed its Mantine migration with a flat data array API, replacing the menu-slot composition pattern entirely.
events.description: Commit 0e6dcebba introduced PdsMantineSelect with Mantine Select, searchable and clearable props, and leading icon support. Documented in repository-archaeology select-mantine-era snippets (screenshot-only on unmerged branch).

events.title: Cross-component fix wave — SelectControlled, Drawer, Modal, React 19
events.summary: A round of cross-component bug fixes addressed SelectControlled stretch behaviour, Drawer auto-height, Modal minimum dimensions, and React 19 peer compatibility — all in response to consumer reports.
events.description: Fixes across May–August 2025: SelectControlled stretch and menu overflow (faa70d3ce, fee625fc1), Drawer height-auto (2c1ad63f4), Modal min-width/height and unique SCSS variables (ad240e9bc, fb5efd1aa), and React 19 peer dependency compatibility (446812eb4).

milestones.title: pds-mcp Server & AI-Assisted Development
milestones.summary: As Tech Lead, I continued shipping Mantine components while the team built AI tooling on top of Podium — an MCP server and LLM docs — and the broader team moved under an AI manager.
milestones.description: pds-mcp server CI job merged Dec 2025 (fe9ff1a1c). LLM docs generator updated for component and icon documentation. Davor shipped MantineTooltip (PDS-201), MantineChip (PDS-182), and MantineAccordion (PDS-22). Maja owned MCP infra, MantineDropdownButton, MantineToggleButton, and icon pipeline. MantineAutocompleteExtended contribution closed the arc Jul 2026.
milestones.outcome: Full Mantine component suite with AI-accessible documentation layer; portfolio-ready repository archaeology and standalone Autocomplete export.
milestones.collaborator_context: Maja Hladnik took ownership of MCP server CI, LLM docs generation, and icon tooling while the broader team transitioned to AI-assisted workflows under an AI manager.

events.title: pds-mcp server CI job merged
events.summary: An MCP server was wired into CI so AI tools could read Podium component docs and help developers use the design system correctly.
events.description: Merge fe9ff1a1c added a GitLab CI job for the pds-mcp server (feat/PDS-misc-add-CI-job-for-MCP). Enabled LLM-accessible component documentation for Cursor and other AI-assisted development tools.

events.title: MantineAccordion (PDS-22)
events.summary: I shipped a full Mantine Accordion family — parent, panel, and control — with Storybook docs, Playwright tests, and LLM documentation.
events.description: feat/PDS-22-Mantine-Accordion merged 991cf6f20. Included PdsMantineAccordion, AccordionControl, AccordionPanel, AccordionItem with intensity surfaces, chevronPosition, multiple/single modes, and comprehensive code snippet tabs.

events.title: MCP LLM docs generator updated
events.summary: The documentation pipeline was updated so AI assistants could consume accurate, versioned component docs from Podium.
events.description: Commit 2c4c51bee updated the LLM docs generator and MCP command, removed unnecessary files, and standardized how component docs are exported for AI consumption.

events.title: MantineTooltip (PDS-201)
events.summary: I built and shipped MantineTooltip with size, intensity, and surface variants — replacing the legacy tooltip with a Mantine-based implementation.
events.description: feat/PDS-201-PdsMantineTooltip merged 0c58ba30c. Included ref-wrapping logic for non-ref children, arrow positioning, Playwright visual regression, LLM docs, and deprecation of the old PdsTooltip.

events.title: MantineChip (PDS-182)
events.summary: I designed and shipped the Chip component family — filter, assist, and input chips — with full Mantine styling and Playwright coverage.
events.description: feat/PDS-182-mantine-chip: PdsChip with color, intensity, leading icon, number badge, dismissible state, dark mode, avatar, and chip group stories. Playwright visual regression and LLM docs completed Feb 2026.

events.title: Maja ships MantineDropdownButton and MantineToggleButton
events.summary: Maja completed the Mantine button family replacements — work she owned independently after mentoring on earlier Mantine components.
events.description: Merges d1acaf58c and e15efe7a0 replaced PdsDropdownButton and PdsToggleButton with Mantine equivalents (PDS-166, PDS-167), including VR tests, LLM docs, and icon color fixes.

events.title: Post-launch Mantine fixes — Accordion, Tooltip, Chip, Code Connect
events.summary: Post-launch fixes across MantineAccordion (intensity surfaces, chevronPosition), MantineTooltip (line-height border), and MantineChip (focus ring outline) — addressing design review feedback after initial merges.
events.description: Design-review and QA fixes Dec 2025–Feb 2026: MantineAccordion panel intensities and chevronPosition (1208bcc6f, 0f893042a), MantineTooltip transparent border for line-height (837f3afce) and design review corrections (42035fb37), MantineChip focus outline (bcfe01461), and MantineAutocomplete Code Connect footer (5d0bda23e).

events.title: MantineAutocompleteExtended — portfolio standalone export
events.summary: I closed the Select/Autocomplete evolution arc with a standalone Autocomplete built for a non-PDS product — portable, token-free, and portfolio-ready.
events.description: Commit e643d9594 added PET MantineAutocompleteExtended contribution and repository archaeologist skill. Final standalone Autocomplete uses Mantine Combobox with extracted SCSS variables (no pds-tokens packages), local Text/Loader primitives, sync/async data, grouped options, and full ARIA. Documented in final-autocomplete snippets.
